summary: 窦武迎立，十二岁即位；窦武陈蕃谋诛宦官败，党锢复炽，西园卖官，黄巾起，东汉之乱自此而始。
summary_en: Raised by Dou Wu, enthroned at twelve; Dou Wu and Chen Fan's plot against the eunuchs failed, the proscription flared again, offices were sold at the West Garden, and the Yellow Turbans rose — the great disorder of Eastern Han began here.

bio_md:
# 汉灵帝 · 主要事迹

刘宏是解渎亭侯刘苌之子。[[e-han-huan|桓帝]]崩而无嗣，窦太后与窦武迎立年十二的刘宏，是为灵帝——东汉末年的序幕，由此拉开。

即位当年，窦武、陈蕃谋诛宦官而事败身死，宦官集团反扑，第二次党锢起，天下名士禁锢者六七百人。此后灵帝的二十余年，宦官与外戚交替掌权，而皇帝本人则把精力投向了另一件事：光和元年开西园卖官，公卿州郡各有定价，「三公」亦可买；同年置鸿都门学，以书画尺牍取士，与太学儒生分庭抗礼。中平二年造万金堂，聚钱西园——汉家四百年基业，在灵帝手中成了可以标价出售的东西。

中平元年，巨鹿张角以太平道聚众，黄巾起义爆发，「八州并起，天下响应」。灵帝赦党人以求合力镇压，命皇甫嵩、朱儁等讨平之，然而州郡牧守之权自此渐重，豪强各自拥兵，汉室之土已呈瓦解之势。中平五年置西园八校尉，袁绍、曹操等皆在其列——这支皇帝亲军，日后将变成群雄争霸的班底。

中平六年，灵帝崩，年三十四。他留下的帝国已千疮百孔：宦官与士人势同水火，黄巾余部遍布州郡，边地军阀虎视眈眈。[[e-han-shao-bian|少帝辩]]即位数月即被董卓所废，东汉遂入末世。

> 参考：点校本《后汉书》卷008《孝灵帝纪》、《党锢列传》、《陈蕃传》、《皇甫嵩传》，谭图第 2 册。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Hong was the son of the marquis Chang of Xieduting.

died without issue, and Empress Dowager Dou with Dou Wu raised the twelve-year-old Hong as Emperor Ling — the curtain rises on the last act of Eastern Han.

In the very first year of his reign, Dou Wu and Chen Fan's plot against the eunuchs failed and cost them their lives; the eunuchs struck back, the second proscription began, and six or seven hundred famous men of the realm were barred from office. For the next twenty years the eunuchs and the consorts took turns at power while the emperor turned his attention elsewhere: in the first Guanghe year he opened office sales at the West Garden, with set prices for dukes, ministers, and provincial governors — even the Three Dukes could be bought; in the same year he founded the Hongdu Academy, choosing scholars for calligraphy and letters against the classicists of the Grand Academy; in the second Zhongping year he built the Hall of Ten Thousand Gold to hoard money at the West Garden. Four hundred years of the Han inheritance had become, in Ling's hands, goods with a price tag.

In the first Zhongping year Zhang Jiao of Julu gathered followers through the Way of Great Peace, and the Yellow Turban revolt erupted — "eight provinces rose together, and the realm answered." Ling lifted the proscription to rally the scholars, and Huangfu Song and Zhu Jun suppressed the revolt; but the power of provincial governors grew from that war, and the regional strongmen each held troops of their own. The realm of Han was already coming apart. In the fifth Zhongping year he created the Eight Colonels of the West Garden, among them Yuan Shao and Cao Cao — this imperial guard would become the roster of the coming warlord age.

In the sixth Zhongping year Ling died at thirty-four, leaving an empire in tatters: eunuchs and scholars at each other's throats, Yellow Turban remnants across the provinces, and frontier warlords closing in.

was deposed by Dong Zhuo within months, and Eastern Han entered its last age.

> References: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hou Hanshu*, ch. 8 (Benji of Emperor Ling), and the biographies of the Proscribed Partisans, Chen Fan, and Huangfu Song; Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2.
